why_the_primary_repo_was_cloneable: The repair branch lives in a linked worktree, but worktrees share the primary repository's ref store, so refs/heads/fix/saathios-full-e2e-functional-recovery was already visible to `git clone`. Nothing was pushed to make this possible.

install.backend_source: the command the private-alpha runbooks already document
install.note: Committed manifests and lockfiles only. No dependency was installed by hand to make the run succeed — where one was missing, the manifest was fixed and the clone rebuilt.

defects_found_by_this_phase.title: The repository could not run its own test suite from committed source
defects_found_by_this_phase.detail: The private-alpha release and rollback runbooks both instruct `pip install -e '.[dev]'`, but no `dev` extra existed and pytest was declared in no manifest at all — only configured via [tool.pytest.ini_options].
defects_found_by_this_phase.resolution: FIXED — pyproject.toml now defines the dev extra with pytest and pytest-asyncio.

defects_found_by_this_phase.title: Three unconditionally-imported modules were undeclared
defects_found_by_this_phase.detail: saathi/agents/master.py, saathi/agents/sub_agents/base.py, saathi/auth_logto.py and saathi/security/redteam/runner.py import groq, jwt and yaml at module scope. groq appeared only in requirements.txt (scoped to cloud deployment); PyJWT and PyYAML appeared nowhere. Five test modules failed to import from a fresh checkout.
defects_found_by_this_phase.resolution: FIXED — declared in pyproject base dependencies, because the imports are not guarded.

defects_found_by_this_phase.title: PyJWT lacked its crypto extra for RS256
defects_found_by_this_phase.detail: saathi/auth_logto.py verifies Logto tokens with jwt.PyJWKClient and algorithms=["RS256"], which needs `cryptography`. Plain PyJWT does not pull it.

defects_found_by_this_phase.title: A fail-closed launcher test never established its own premise
defects_found_by_this_phase.detail: test_launcher_still_fails_closed_when_backend_must_spawn_without_venv pointed SAATHI_REPO at a directory it never created. bin/saathi-local:_resolve_repo only honours SAATHI_REPO when it contains saathi-os/, so the override was silently ignored, the launcher resolved the real repository, found the .venv the documentation tells you to create, and the assertion was never reached. It passed only on machines without a .venv.
defects_found_by_this_phase.resolution: FIXED — the test now builds a fake repo with saathi-os/ and deliberately no .venv, mirroring the sibling frontend test. Strengthened, not weakened: verified by mutation — replacing the `[ -x "$PY" ]` guard in bin/saathi-local with a no-op makes it fail. bin/saathi-local itself is unchanged.

authentication_bypass_probe.verdict: bypass remains closed in a clean clone built only from committed source

observations_investigated_not_defects.observation: First browser attempt on port 3777 scored 81/86 with 168 console errors, all CORS-blocked
observations_investigated_not_defects.finding: NOT_A_DEFECT — saathi/cors_policy.py enforces a fixed allowlist of local dev origins (3000, 3100, 3110, 3112, 8765). Port 3777 is not on it, so the backend correctly refused the origin. A strict origin allowlist is the right behaviour; the port choice was wrong. Rerun on the allowlisted 3110: 86/86.

observations_investigated_not_defects.observation: Clean clone shows 51 console errors and 25 failed requests vs 1 and 0 in the repair worktree
observations_investigated_not_defects.finding: NOT_A_DEFECT, and the clean clone is the stricter of the two. 24 of the 25 are one shell widget polling the legacy /api/v1/connectors/approvals/pending, which the clean clone answers 401 while the repair worktree answers 200. Cause: saathi/server.py reads BAADAR_PASSWORD at import; _is_authed falls back to trusting loopback only when no password is configured. The app auto-writes a .env with a generated BAADAR_PASSWORD on first run. The repair worktree's backend started at 06:59:43, before its .env was written at 07:57:18, so it runs with an empty password and trusts loopback. The clean clone started after its own .env existed, so legacy endpoints correctly require a legacy session that the platform-only browser cert never establishes. All 86 platform assertions pass in both. .env is gitignored and was never committed.

observations_investigated_not_defects.observation: Clean clone skips 7 tests, the repair worktree skips 1
observations_investigated_not_defects.finding: EXPECTED — every skip is an optional-dependency or opt-in guard, enumerated with -rs: test_generation.py:51 'slow render; set SAATHI_SLOW=1' (the same opt-in skip the repair worktree has); test_m17_2_native.py x5 'PyObjC unavailable'; test_voice_os.py:188 'faster_whisper not installed'. PyObjC and faster-whisper live in the [voice] extra, which `pip install -e '.[dev]'` deliberately does not install. No skip was introduced by this branch and none masks a failure.
